title: KV preemption, soft-failover and batch contraction protocol for OOM resilience
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Goal: implement a coordinated protocol combining continuous batching admission control, KV-cache preemption heuristics, and a batch-contraction fallback path to prevent GPU OOMs while minimizing latency and quality degradation. This ticket covers the design, prototype, and canary rollout for a runtime-level 'soft-failover' that: 1) preempts low-priority KV entries proactively when headroom dips below a moving threshold, 2) contracts in-flight batches (drop lower-priority requests or shorten context) to keep latency SLOs, and 3) transparently routes overflow requests to a lighter fallback model or a reduced-fidelity execution path with retries and exponential backoff.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controlled canary: in Dedicated pool canary fleet, OOM incidents reduce to zero for synthetic workload with intermittent long-context spikes without more than 15% request-level fidelity downgrades.
2) Observability: new metrics (kv_preempt_count, batch_contract_count, fallback_route_rate, oom_incidents) are emitted and visible in Console for canary pods.
3) Latency: p95 token latency for high-priority routes increases by <=10% during failover.
4) Correctness: requests routed to fallback model must include diagnostic headers and be retriable by client with consistent error codes.
5) Automation: rollout policy can enable/disable protocol via Console toggle and respect per-customer pinning to disable automatic fallback.
technical_notes:
- KV preemption uses per-tenant LRU+priority buckets with a soft TTL; eviction is signalled via a lightweight 'preempt intent' which allows the batch admission layer to account for imminent memory reclaim.
- Admission controller maintains a moving-window estimate of GPU free bytes; thresholds: GREEN (>8% free), YELLOW (3-8%), RED (<3%). Preemption starts at YELLOW, batch contraction enforced at RED.
- Batch contraction options (ordered by preference): 1) trim trailing context tokens (cheap), 2) convert sampling params to single-shot greedy for low-priority requests, 3) drop queued low-priority requests with NACK and retry advice, 4) route to micro-quantized fallback model (same architecture, 4-bit) with best-effort KV warmstart.
- Fallback routing preserves request metadata and injects X-Redwood-Fallback and X-Redwood-Fidelity headers.
- Memory accounting uses a combination of model-slot reservation and live allocation watermarking; we add a small hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Trade-offs considered: eager preemption increases cold-cache penalties for subsequent requests; aggressive batch contraction hurts PLG customers with mixed priority workloads. We favor conservative preemption + prioritized contraction to protect high-priority requests.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (prototype): implement kv_preempt_intent signal and admission hook (2 wks). Add metric emission and flags.
Phase 2 (integration): implement batch contraction strategies and fallback routing + fidelity headers (3 wks).
Phase 3 (canary): run on 5% Dedicated capacity for synthetic spike scenario and iterate (2 wks).
Phase 4 (rollout): enable in progressive steps and add console toggle + per-customer opt-out (1 wk).
Phase 5 (post-rollout): collect metrics, perf regressions, and iterate on thresholds (ongoing).
rollout_plan: Canary on dedicated-small pool (5% capacity) for 2 weeks with synthetic spike harness and a few opt-in customers. Monitor oom_incidents and fallback_route_rate. If fallback_route_rate > 20% for any customer, auto-disable for that customer and open follow-up ticket. Provide a Console feature flag and API toggle to opt out. Final enablement gated by QA signoff and SRE runbook update.
qa_plan:
- Synthetic workloads: long-context generator with variable request priority to validate preemption and contraction behavior.
- Chaos test: inject artificial allocation noise to reproduce OOM and confirm graceful degradation path.
- Regression: run existing batching throughput benchmarks and compare p50/p95 latency and token throughput.
- Integration: validate headers/trace continuity between primary and fallback model runs.
open_questions:
1) Should preemption prefer tenant-local KV entries or global shared entries when memory is scarce? (engineering/ops decision)
2) What is the acceptable SLA for requests that are downgraded to fallback (percent of tokens identical or semantic similarity threshold)?
3) Are there customers that must never be transparently routed to fallback (compliance/legal)? We need a per-customer policy schema.
4) How does this interact with existing autoscaler/eviction; do we coordinate signals with node-level OOM killer?
decisions:
2026-02-24: Adopted moving-window headroom thresholds (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) and conservative preemption at YELLOW.
2026-03-03: Batch contraction prioritizes context trimming > sampling simplification > dropping low-priority requests.
2026-03-09: Fallback models must be explicitly registered in model-catalog with fidelity metadata and opt-out labels.
